presentation.more: `getAnnotation` is documented to answer nothing in ordinary conditions — an unset variable, the end of a stream, a path that is not there — and the type this function sees does not say so, so the compiler lets it dereference the answer unchecked. When the answer is absent, the first member access throws. Test the answer, or supply a default, before using it.

finding.message: A failure is caught and cannot be reported. The failure is caught and nothing is returned, so callers get the same value whether the work failed or succeeded. The work is silently lost.

presentation.description: The failure is caught and nothing is returned, so callers get the same value whether the work failed or succeeded. The work is silently lost.

derivedFacts: the handler neither rethrows nor records the failure anywhere a caller can read
this function returns nothing, so failing and succeeding look identical to a caller
callers in this project exist, and every one of them is told the work succeeded
reachableWhen: whenever the work inside the `try` fails

presentation.more: This catches the failure and carries on, and it returns nothing — so a caller has no way to find out. "It failed and I dropped it" and "it worked" arrive at every caller as the same value, however carefully that caller is written, and the work is simply lost. Logging it does not fix this: the log is not where the caller is. Give this method an answer the caller can act on, or let the failure out to whoever awaits it — rethrowing into a call nobody awaits is an unhandled rejection, not a report.

finding.message: A request to stop is caught and ignored. The handler catches the cancellation signal and carries on, so cancelled work runs to the end. Whoever asked it to stop cannot tell that it did not.

presentation.description: The handler catches the cancellation signal and carries on, so cancelled work runs to the end. Whoever asked it to stop cannot tell that it did not.

derivedFacts: the handler's type catches the cancellation signal
cancellation can reach the protected code
the handler neither rethrows nor restores the request
reachableWhen: whenever the work is cancelled while this runs

presentation.more: This handler catches the platform's cancellation signal — by its own type or through a supertype — and carries on, so a request to stop becomes an instruction to keep going: the cancelled work runs to the end, whoever cancelled it waits for a completion that no longer means anything, and nothing further up can see that a stop was asked for. Let the cancellation out (rethrow it, or catch a narrower type), or on the JVM restore the interrupt with `Thread.currentThread().interrupt()` before carrying on.
